cheats.name: Stop Time
cheats.note: FixedUpdate only advances timeOfDay while timeFactor < 10; the game sets 50 when closed/day ends and 1.0 on open (AuxiliarSupermarketOpen). Freezing 50 halts the clock. Read from GameData disassembly; not run in-game. Host only (SyncVar).

cheats.name: Time Speed x2
cheats.note: timeOfDay += (1/timeFactor)*dt/60 while open, normal 1.0. Use only while open: while closed, a value < 10 starts the clock. Untested for the day-end path. Read from GameData disassembly; not run in-game. Host only (SyncVar).

cheats.name: Time Speed x4
cheats.note: See Time Speed x2. Never use 0 (divide by zero). Read from GameData disassembly; not run in-game. Host only (SyncVar).

cheats.name: Fast Shopping (customers grab instantly, move much faster)
cheats.note: NPC_Info.productItemPlaceWait (+0x208, per-customer, no singleton) is computed once at spawn as Mathf.Clamp(0.5 - gameDay*0.003, 0.1, 0.5) then stored here; <PlaceProductsCoroutine>d__137.MoveNext reads it back as the per-item grab delay (traced live this session). No global field to freeze, so this scales the value written at spawn instead. Signature verified unique live; the arm/patch mechanism itself was not run in-game.

cheats.name: Fast Checkout (employee + self-checkout)
cheats.note: Merges the three checkout-wait fields (employee cashier: +0x2C4 live 0.4s; self-checkout min/max: +0x2C8/+0x2CC live 0.85s/1.75s) into one toggle. captureOriginal (not a shared offValue) so each target restores its own live value on disable, since the three defaults differ. Employee wait traced by name only; self-checkout waits traced live into <CustomerSelfCheckout>d__139.MoveNext this session. Not run in-game.

cheats.name: Fast Shopping companion: customer NavMeshAgent speed
cheats.note: NPC_Manager.SetAgentData(agent) runs once per customer at spawn (called from <SpawnCustomerNPC>d__203.MoveNext) and makes 4-5 property-setter calls on the passed-in component in sequence: a bool (true), then floats with day-scaled-and-clamped values -- 1.0 flat, ~1.9+small growth, 120+up to 60, 8+up to 24. Never confirmed which Unity API each setter is (no icall names visible, only JIT thunk addresses) -- identified the 3rd float setter (~1.9-6 range) as NavMeshAgent.speed by numeric plausibility against Unity's own defaults (speed ~1-6, angularSpeed default 120, acceleration default 8, which the 4th and 5th setters' ranges match almost exactly). This is the best guess, not a confirmed mechanism. Anchored on the instruction right after the final cvtsd2ss produces the float (xmm1) and before the property-setter call consumes it, so the multiply applies to the same value regardless of which property it turns out to be. Signature verified unique live; not armed in-game. Hidden as a companion of stm-fast-shopping (kind:patch + internal) rather than a separate toggle, since the user asked for one Fast Shopping switch.
